objectives: Buy museum tickets and ask about discounts
Find the cloakroom and the audio guide

teach.note: la entrada = museum or show ticket (and entrance). A transport ticket is el billete.

teach.en: Is there a discount for students?
teach.note: At the Prado, under-18s and students aged 18–25 go free at any time. They still need a timed ticket, and students need a valid student card. Over-65s pay less. Other museums vary, so ask.

teach.md:
**The Prado.** Open **10:00–20:00** Monday to Saturday, and **10:00–19:00** on Sundays.

**La entrada gratuita** (free entry) is the last two hours: **18:00–20:00** Monday to Saturday, **17:00–19:00** on Sundays.

- Those are the most crowded hours. **La cola** (the queue) is often 60–90 minutes long.
- Even free entry needs a ticket with a time slot. Free-hours tickets are handed out at the **taquilla** on the day, so you can't just walk in.
- On a short trip, a paid timed ticket (€15) bought online can be worth it: you skip the queue and choose your time.

The Reina Sofía (Guernica) is closed on Tuesdays.

teach.es: ¿Dónde está la cola para la entrada gratuita?
teach.en: Where's the queue for free entry?
teach.note: la cola = the queue. Hacer cola = to queue. Gratis also means free: la entrada es gratis.
Big bags and backpacks have to go to the guardarropa. It's free.
Ask: ¿La tienen en inglés? But try the Spanish one for a room or two.

teach.es: ¿Se pueden hacer fotos? — En el Prado, no.
teach.en: Can you take photos? — Not in the Prado.
teach.note: hacer fotos = to take photos (Spain). Photos aren't allowed in the Prado's galleries. Other museums vary, so ask.

vocab.note: el descuento = discount. ¿Hay descuento para estudiantes?
Masculine, even though it ends in -a.
